# R0005: Route prefetched and late prayer responses correctly across civil midnight

**Repository-local identity:** `R0005` in `theislampill/salah_widget`; existing tracker [#5](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/5). The SW identifier is historical draft provenance.


Campaign draft alias: SW-005. Existing corrective owner: GitHub #5. Proposed priority P1; product-or-skill defect. This work order specifies day adoption and its consumer invalidation; it does not authorize implementation or publish a repair.

## Three connected transitions, one owner

On main `fd2972ba64225fe9d6848e92497e6d0ed20ea624`, tomorrow's already-completed data is discarded when the loop notices midnight. In the recorded UTC September 7→8 fixture, the widget had today=September 7/Hijri 19 and tomorrow=September 8/Hijri 20. After Maghrib it displayed Hijri 20; offline midnight discarded tomorrow and retained September 7, so the display went backward to stale Hijri 19. Candidate `9d9c43649748555afbe09e3ca49bc47db2d7e7bb` checks the prefetched Gregorian date, promotes September 8 and retains Hijri 20. That completed-promotion patch is a useful control.

A different scheduling witness fails on **both** trees. At September 7 23:59:59, dispatch tomorrow=September 8 and hold its promise. Cross midnight and let a rollover request load September 8. Release the older prefetch. Both end with `today.date=tomorrow.date="08-09-2026"`, never request September 9, and fail the next Maghrib advance; the candidate nevertheless reports `maghribRollApplied=true`. The callback assigns according to its original name “tomorrow,” even though its payload has become today. Promoting only records already completed at midnight does not repair that callback.

HA-N002 records the final transition: successful asynchronous new-day adoption can update data without causing a render. With a frozen simulation second, the displayed old date/stale flag remained through 20 callbacks. With ordinary advancing seconds, the next second repairs the sampled discrepancy. Therefore the supported claim is an adoption→consumer invalidation failure, not a guaranteed visible flash in every normal load.

These are retained exact-source controlled fixtures, not new browser runs or a claim about all Islamic calendar conventions. DATE-002, DATE-004 and HA-N002 are owned together because an admitted day must be placed in the right slot and become visible. Hijri date-selection/hold policy remains [R0009](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/9).

## Re-anchor and causal owner

Record actual checkout, HEAD and dirty state using `git -C C:\workspace\ai\salah_widget rev-parse --show-toplevel`, `rev-parse HEAD`, `status --short`, and `diff -- index.html tests/smoke.html` with that same prefix. Stop for relevant incompatible drift. Inspect [main prefetch callback](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/blob/fd2972ba64225fe9d6848e92497e6d0ed20ea624/index.html#L1986-L1990), [main midnight/adoption/render gate](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/blob/fd2972ba64225fe9d6848e92497e6d0ed20ea624/index.html#L2232-L2262), and [candidate completed promotion](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/blob/9d9c43649748555afbe09e3ca49bc47db2d7e7bb/index.html#L2321-L2353).

The existing `tomorrowStr()` increments a UTC-constructed civil date. Saved month/year/leap/DST controls passed on both trees. Its replacement with epoch+86400000 would introduce a separate bug. Preserve the actual calendar operation and define today/tomorrow by local civil identity at **adoption**, not 24-hour elapsed duration.

## Adoption contract and precise state table

The immutable context from [R0003](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/3) establishes which configuration and operation still own the completion. Admission from [R0002](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/2) establishes that payload Gregorian identity equals its requested date. Only then classify it against `nowParts()` in the resolved location zone. Proposed design pseudocode below names decisions, not a new externally exposed schema:

```text
currentDay = location civil day at adoption
nextDay    = civil successor of currentDay
payloadDay = admitted response Gregorian day
obsolete generation/slot -> no adoption; settle only its own operation
payloadDay == currentDay -> eligible for today
payloadDay == nextDay    -> eligible for tomorrow
otherwise               -> no current/tomorrow adoption
```

| Before/completion | Required transition |
|---|---|
| Completed prefetched record now matches currentDay | Promote it to today **before** clearing tomorrow; persist under its actual date, clear stale, invalidate consumers. |
| In-flight prefetch becomes currentDay, today is absent/stale | Adopt as today; clear only matching old tomorrow state; release its own prefetch slot; allow nextDay acquisition. |
| Late prefetch becomes currentDay, a newer valid current record is already installed | Treat it as a duplicate no-op for today; do not overwrite the newer record or populate tomorrow with currentDay. Settle its own slot. |
| Prefetch still equals nextDay | Install as tomorrow if its context/operation remains eligible; current today stays intact; invalidate Hijri/Fajr consumers. |
| Completion arrives after an additional day of sleep or a backward date correction | If neither currentDay nor nextDay, discard from live slots. If it matches one, use that classification; an old dispatch label is not authority. |
| No matching cache/prefetch at a day transition | Retain old today only with stale state; leave current day unaccepted and recovery eligible under the bounded retry owner. |

1. Consolidate the repeated assignment bundle at the existing loader/prefetch/rollover boundaries: accepted payload and actual day, cache key from context, `lastDate`, stale flag, matching tomorrow clear/promotion, moon/star date invalidation and render-dirty signal. A narrow adoption function is justified only if those real callers use it. Do not move acquisition, provider validation, Hijri policy and all rendering into a generic state framework.
2. At midnight, test the completed prefetched record's admitted day and generation before consulting the current-day cache. Adopt the matching record before assigning `tomorrow=null`. Preserve valid cache fallback and the existing bounded offline retry opportunity. Never advance the accepted-day marker merely because the wall clock crossed; it advances only when current data was accepted. Any separate loop “observed day” marker must not suppress retries after a failed adoption.
3. Replace the unconditional prefetch `.then(d=>{tomorrow=d;...})` with the state table. Do the current-day/current-generation check after the promise settles. A current valid `today` obtained from a later rollover operation wins over a now-duplicate late prefetch; this avoids unnecessary stale-over-fresh replacement without inventing provider timestamps. Clear/release only the old operation's slot. A prior operation may not clear a newer prefetch busy state, per the ownership contract.
4. Reset prefetch eligibility by configuration and requested civil day through [R0006](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/6)'s scheduler state. Do not reset the cooldown every render or block September 9 because a non-null tomorrow happens to contain September 8. A valid nextDay record suppresses redundant requests; an invalid/wrong-day tomorrow slot does not. Successful promotion must leave the system capable of fetching the new nextDay.
5. Use a single coalesced render-dirty flag at accepted asynchronous state changes. The existing visible rAF loop renders when its simulated second changes **or** state is dirty, then consumes that dirty flag. A completion while hidden marks dirty; the first visible callback paints it without creating a second rAF loop. Keep existing explicit initial loader render where needed before loop startup. Do not call `render()` recursively from `model()` or every promise callback. Mark only after eligible adoption, not after rejected/obsolete results.
6. Preserve candidate moon/star invalidation details where the accepted day changes: `_starsProjected=false`, appropriate moon re-render/stamp invalidation and `lastMoonMin` reset. Those are consumers of an adopted day; arbitrary new celestial animation is out of scope. Preserve opaque calendar moon and the existing visible-motion/reduced-motion contract.

Rejected alternatives matter here. Unconditionally clearing tomorrow cures neither late callbacks nor offline loss. Rejecting all responses dispatched before midnight throws away useful current-day data. A global “date never decreases” rule would hide backward device corrections and provider anomalies; it cannot establish current Gregorian identity. Rendering from every callback creates repeated work and can recurse into another prefetch; one invalidation consumed by the existing loop is sufficient.

## Deterministic RED, GREEN and mutation controls

Build a disposable controlled-clock fixture using actual prefetch callback and `startRenderLoop`, with in-memory fetch/cache and paint capture. Synthetic record `P(day,hijriDay)` has matching Gregorian fields, UTC metadata, six usable clocks Fajr 05:00, Sunrise 06:00, Dhuhr 12:00, Asr 15:30, Maghrib/Sunset 18:00, Isha 19:30, and Hijri year 1448/month 2 with the supplied day. These dates/times are fixture inputs, not a provider calendar claim.

| Recipe | Required observable final result |
|---|---|
| Start `2026-09-07T23:59:59Z`, today=P(7,19), completed tomorrow=P(8,20), network offline; advance 2 seconds | today/lastDate September 8, stale false, persisted September 8, current Hijri selection 20 under existing Maghrib policy. Historical main produced stale September 7/Hijri 19; candidate promotion is the useful positive branch. |
| Same start, hold first request for September 8; cross midnight, release rollover September 8, then release old prefetch September 8 | today September 8; tomorrow is absent or September 9, never September 8; old response does not replace newer accepted data; September 9 becomes requestable. Advance through next Maghrib and observe its correct next-day consumer. |
| Release prefetch September 8 after midnight while rollover fails | Late response may repair current today, clear stale, and persist its actual day. Blanket rejection of pre-midnight requests fails this control. |
| Release normally before midnight | Store September 8 only in tomorrow, keep September 7 today, preserve pre-Maghrib preview and later Maghrib selection. |
| Switch configuration before old completion; or release September 8 after current day September 9 | No old-generation mutation; no stale September 8 installed as current/tomorrow on September 9; owning current operation remains busy until its own completion. |
| Frozen `simTime`, stale old record, release a valid current-day response after the last paint | The **first next visible frame** consumes dirty state and paints adopted day/stale=false without changing simulated seconds; 20 further callbacks cannot retain old output or produce redundant per-frame fetches. Hide before release and verify the first resumed frame. |
| Year/month/leap controls | Keep Dec 31→Jan 1, Feb 28 2024→Feb 29→Mar 1 and New York DST civil-next-day results. No arithmetic replacement by fixed elapsed 24h. |

Capture request dates, operation IDs, loaded/next-day slots, accepted date, stale flag, selected/displayed date and cache writes at every release point. A final screenshot alone can miss a poisoned tomorrow slot; a final state number alone can miss a frozen consumer. Browser date/status crops must supplement source witnesses. Temporarily disable promotion, restore unconditional tomorrow assignment, and disable render-dirty consumption separately in an authorized isolated fixture: each matching test must fail. Restore final source before qualifying it.

## Integration and closeable boundary

Accepted interface predecessors are [R0003](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/3) for requesting-context ownership and [R0004](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/4) for location-day boot; [R0002](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/2) supplies final valid-day qualification. This owner supplies current/promotion state to [R0009](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/9). Shared production hunks with [R0006](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/6) (eligibility/retry) and [R0020](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/32) (forward/backward current instant) require one integrator, not competing edits to the loop. Preserve the existing relationship graph; a common `index.html` does not make every other issue a predecessor.

Change the adoption/callback/render-invalidation paths and their invoked fixtures. Update DESIGN/HANDOFF or README where they explain midnight, retained stale data or frozen-scene refresh; do not claim a new prayer calculation or Hijri authority. Main cache identity, builder/config output, install scripts and presets remain compatible. The public surface is a correct current day and responsive date consumer within the existing readable 325×530 card.

If candidate promotion is integrated but late prefetch or frozen repaint still fails, record that partial state and keep #5 open. Revert the coordinated day assignments/invalidation changes if valid cache, ordinary prefetch or rendering regresses; preserve old cache bytes and failure evidence. Acceptance requires final-tree transition/control results, independent review of caller reachability, and actual rendered readback before an evidence comment and manual closure. Use non-closing `Implements #5`; served-source/readback is additionally required for deployment claims. Supplementary historical companion SHA256: `2c7bf3fff141c5d1d9fd5f7b4ad3a6aaa4ee1d7159bfb075eae54b30f0da42ec`. The decisive public inputs above do not require the private companion.

Identity provenance: first repository-local allocation batch; existing GitHub object order was used to assign distinct monotonic hex-4 IDs. Closed/held IDs are not reused. Issue number is not implementation priority.
